rules.statement: Model a vocabulary that a consumer, deployment or sibling package could ever need to extend as `public const string` names in a static class, compared ordinally and documented as the known values, not as an `enum`.
rules.why: Open vocabularies keep the library extensible; an enum fixes its members at compile time, and only editing the defining package can open it again.
rules.check: Look for a new public `enum` whose members a different package could reasonably want to add to, such as reasons, formats, entity kinds or scopes. Also flag name comparisons that are not ordinal.

rules.statement: Introduce an `enum` only when its members are fixed by something outside extension: a finite enumeration of an external specification implemented in full, the outcome set of one library-owned operation, or a mirror of a framework type. No other package could need another member, and a new member would require a library change anyway.
rules.why: Asking whether the package owns today's members misleads authors. The test is whether a package that is not this one could ever need to add a member.
rules.check: For each new enum, check whether the PR or its docs give the three-part justification. Flag enums justified only by the library owning the current members.

rules.statement: Do not use `[Flags]` for a vocabulary that may grow.
rules.why: A flags enum fixes the bit space and the meaning of every combination, which closes the vocabulary even further.
rules.check: Flag new `[Flags]` enums whose members represent extensible concepts, such as scopes, entity types or capabilities.

rules.statement: Never encode relationships among a vocabulary's members (hierarchy, cascade, compatibility, order) in a `switch`, bit mask or hard-coded chain. Declare them as registered data and let a catalog derive them.
rules.why: Hard-coded relationships close the behavior and topology even when the member names are strings, so extensions cannot take part.
rules.check: Look for a `switch` statement or expression, a mask, or an if-chain over vocabulary members that returns a parent, a next item, an order or a compatibility answer.

rules.statement: Do not choose behavior with an exhaustive `switch` over an open vocabulary. Dispatch to a strategy registered by name through a DI strategy collection or `ICollectionDataSource<T>`.
rules.why: Hard-coded dispatch means a member added by another package has no behavior and cannot get any.
rules.check: Flag a `switch` over string-name constants or a growable enum that picks an implementation. Expect a lookup by name in a resolved collection instead.

rules.statement: When vocabulary members carry behavior or relationships, resolve them through a catalog that validates the whole registered set when it is composed: duplicate names, dangling references and cycles.
rules.why: Registered data from many packages can conflict or form invalid graphs, and composing the catalog is when to catch that.
rules.check: Look at a new catalog or registry built from registered descriptors. Flag one that does not check for duplicate names, references to unregistered members, or cycles.

rules.statement: Reject input that names an unregistered vocabulary member instead of ignoring it or falling back to a default.
rules.why: An open vocabulary is still closed to unregistered input. Silently ignoring an unknown name hides errors and fails open.
rules.check: Flag a name lookup that skips unknown names, returns null without raising an error, or uses a default branch for an unrecognized value.

rules.statement: Persist or send a vocabulary value as its name, never as an enum ordinal or integer value.
rules.why: An older node that meets a newer member then fails closed by name instead of misreading a number.
rules.check: Flag enum values stored in database columns or JSON as integers, `(int)` casts written to storage, and serializers set up without string enum conversion for persisted or wire data.
